meta.scene_summary: We are building the future on top of abandoned GitHub tokens and someone else's anxiety.

cooking.headline: OpenAI is turning your chatbot into a digital billboard
cooking.summary: OpenAI is introducing sponsored agents, meaning your favorite AI assistant is about to start pitching products in the middle of a brainstorm. It is the digital equivalent of someone interrupting your group project meeting to sell you a timeshare.
cooking.plain_english: OpenAI is adding a feature that allows companies to create advertisements within ChatGPT interactions.

cooking.headline: Claude finally realizes that talking to your coworkers and working are the same thing
cooking.summary: Anthropic merged their chat and coworker modes because apparently, having two separate apps was just another form of multitasking we didn't need. It's the digital equivalent of finally realizing your project manager and your therapist are actually the same person.
cooking.plain_english: Anthropic has combined its conversational AI and its task-oriented AI agent into a single platform.

cooking.headline: Gemini 3.8 now has 'Extended Thinking' so it can stress about your prompt even longer
cooking.summary: Google added an extended thinking mode to Gemini, which is exactly how I act when a recruiter asks me where I see myself in five years. It's great that the model can now pause to ponder, but I'm not sure I want my AI to have the same existential crisis I have during a code review.
cooking.plain_english: Google has released an updated version of its Gemini AI model that includes a feature allowing it to perform more intensive analysis before responding.

cooked.headline: Salesforce just took the day off without telling anyone
cooked.summary: Salesforce is experiencing a global outage, leaving everyone to remember what it's like to actually manually track a lead. It turns out that when the CRM goes down, the entire sales department just becomes a group of people staring at their phones waiting for a sign.
cooked.plain_english: Salesforce is currently experiencing a widespread technical failure that has made its services inaccessible to users globally.

cooked.headline: The 'Cloud' is actually just someone else's computer in a warzone
cooked.summary: AWS confirmed some data in Middle Eastern facilities is permanently lost due to physical strikes, proving that 'the cloud' is definitely still susceptible to terrestrial physics. It's a harsh reminder that your off-site backup strategy might need to include 'geo-political stability' as a requirement.
cooked.plain_english: Amazon Web Services reported that it is unable to recover certain data from its data centers in the Middle East following physical damage caused by military strikes.

cooked.headline: Hugging Face is sending OpenAI a $100M invoice for 'hacking'
cooked.summary: OpenAI reportedly scraped Hugging Face's compute traces, and now they're being hit with a bill that feels like a massive restaurant tab for a meal they didn't order. It turns out that when you scrape everyone else's data, you eventually run into the one company that knows exactly how much your data-mining cost them.
cooked.plain_english: Hugging Face is demanding $100 million from OpenAI, claiming the company scraped their platform's data without permission.

cooked.headline: Google really out here doing the 'copy my homework' meme for real
cooked.summary: Google allegedly copied open-source code and scrubbed the original authors' names, which is the corporate equivalent of taking credit for a group project you didn't contribute to. It's a bold strategy to act like you invented the wheel while the people who actually built it are still in the repo history.
cooked.plain_english: Google is accused of using open-source code in their projects while failing to properly credit the original developers.

cooked.headline: Baseten gave away the keys to the castle via a forgotten GitHub token
cooked.summary: Security researchers found a hardcoded GitHub token that essentially handed them the keys to Baseten's entire production environment. It turns out that 'move fast and break things' shouldn't include leaving your admin credentials in the public repo.
cooked.plain_english: Security researchers gained full access to Baseten's internal systems because a developer accidentally left a sensitive digital key in a public code repository.

cooked.headline: The cameras watching everyone else just got caught looking at themselves
cooked.summary: Security researchers managed to hack into Flock's surveillance cameras, proving that even the systems designed to track everyone have their own security blind spots. It's the ultimate 'who watches the watchmen' plot twist, only with more SQL injection.
cooked.plain_english: Hackers identified vulnerabilities in Flock's security cameras that allowed them to access the system's data and control features.

cooked.headline: Microsoft is worried their AI rival might be too good at being a person
cooked.summary: Microsoft is officially concerned that Anthropic's AI could pose a disastrous threat to humanity. It is truly peak corporate irony to watch the company that shipped Clippy worry about another bot's impact on our collective sanity.
cooked.plain_english: Microsoft has expressed concerns that the AI technology developed by Anthropic could potentially cause significant harm to society.
